- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent peak), apply a 3–5 day lag correction to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5–10% from recent peak), model should adjust downward by 2–4% in next forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.2–0.4) over 5+ days, forecast should be capped at 1–2% below recent 10-day average to avoid prolonged underestimation.
